business_scope.primary_industry_name: Virtual Performance Hosting and Digital Ticket Tokenization

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1992 (Cap. 222) of the Republic of Vanuatu, as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2012, ss. 2-18 (incorporation, memorandum and articles, registered office and registered agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registry, Port Vila, Vanuatu
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association of an International Company, filed with the application for registration under the International Companies Act 1992
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up or authorized capital; no escrowed capital deposit or capital verification required by Vanuatu law; an International Company may issue shares with or without par value in any currency
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscribers present are allotted the initial ordinary shares set out in the register of members, and payment for such shares is recorded as received by the Company; (2) the registered office in Port Vila, Vanuatu, established through the licensed registered agent, is adopted as the Company’s statutory registered office; (3) the first directors are appointed and hold office until removal or resignation; (4) any director may execute documents, open bank accounts and instruct advisers to complete registration; (5) the directors are authorised to establish corporate records and affix the common seal; and (6) the minutes of this meeting shall be adopted as true and accurate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Port Vila
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation request with the VFSC Companies Registry through a licensed registered agent. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, trade mark or restricted term. Pay the published name reservation fee and await an electronic name approval letter.
required_dossiers: Brief explanation or purpose of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file three alternate name options. VFSC will reserve the first eligible name; the original refusal does not require a new application fee when alternate names are submitted within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Registered Agent and Preparation of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Vanuatu registered agent (service provider authorised by VFSC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a VFSC-licensed registered agent and instruct them to prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association, consent of director, registered office notification and resolution documents. The registered agent must verify the true identity of shareholders and directors and keep client due-diligence records at the registered office in Vanuatu.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copy of each shareholder and director
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank reference)
Bank reference letter or source of wealth statement
Signed engagement letter with the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent queries any beneficial-owner information, provide a corrected declaration and supporting evidence within seven days. The agent will re-certify the file and continue the filing without restarting incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment of Filing Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Memorandum and Articles of Association, notice of registered office and registered agent, consent to act as director, and certified statutory forms through the licensed agent’s e-Registry account. Pay the official state filing fee at VFSC and retain the payment receipt.
required_dossiers: Notice of registered office and registered agent
Statement of no disqualification by director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC issues a query, the registered agent must correct the relevant form and resubmit within 14 calendar days. If the query is purely administrative, no additional filing fee is charged; substantive changes may require a nominal amendment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, VFSC will register the company and issue a Certificate of Incorporation in the name of the International Company. Collect the certified copy of the certificate, constitutional documents and register of members. The Directors may authorise a common seal, if desired.
required_dossiers: Registered agent confirmation of filing date
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical error, submit the original certificate and a written rectification request to VFSC. The registry will issue a corrected certificate within three business days without re-examining the merits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolutions and Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors of the International Company with the VFSC-registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or pass written consent resolutions to approve the allotment of shares, adopt the registered office, appoint directors and approve the issue of share certificates. The minutes and registers must be kept at the registered office in Port Vila and updated in the company’s minute book.
required_dossiers: First board meeting minutes or unanimous board consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC later requests a copy of board records for its statutory register, provide a conformed copy certified by the registered agent. Late creation or amendment of the record is remedied by a written directors’ resolution ratified at the next board meeting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – the virtual concert and metaverse ticketing business has no physical establishment in Vanuatu; a physical studio, if opened, would require registration with the Vanuatu Department of Industry / VFSC Business Licence Office
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required – no statutory manufacturing, securities or event-venue operating licence applies to virtual performance hosting and USDC/Stripe digital ticketing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Vanuatu Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – digital-only service, no physical construction, discharge or land disturbance
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No VOCs, wastewater effluent or hazardous waste generated; virtual infrastructure relies on third-party cloud hosting using ISO 14001-aligned data-centre controls, and any obligor data-centre has separate host-country compliance

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for remote virtual operations. If a Vanuatu office or event studio is subsequently opened, obtain a Fire Safety Certificate from the Vanuatu Fire and Emergency Services, a structural load inspection from Port Vila Municipal Council and an occupational health clearance for all on-site workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Revenue and Customs Department (VRCD), Ministry of Finance and Economic Management; official tax portal: https://vrcd.gov.vu; corporate registry regulator: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the International Company (IC) with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) under the International Companies Act [Cap 222]; VFSC issues the Certificate of Incorporation and company number. Step 2: Apply to the Vanuatu Revenue and Customs Department (VRCD) for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) using the non-resident taxpayer registration form together with certified incorporation documents, registered agent details, and director/ultimate beneficial ownership declarations. Step 3: Assess VAT registration obligation under the Value Added Tax Act [Cap 246]: register for VAT using Form VAT-01 if taxable supplies equal or exceed VT 5,000,000 in any twelve-month period, or voluntarily if the IC makes only zero-rated offshore digital supplies; VRCD issues the VAT registration certificate and VAT identification number. Step 4: Submit the IC annual return to VFSC confirming no Vanuatu-resident business activity or local asset holdings, and maintain ongoing VAT filings even where all supplies are zero-rated exports.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — A Vanuatu International Company is statutorily exempt from all income, corporate, capital gains, withholding, and stamp taxes under section 47 of the International Companies Act [Cap 222]. Vanuatu levies no national income tax, so the IC is not a pass-through in the traditional sense; it is a tax-exempt offshore vehicle. VAT is a distinct consumption tax: the IC becomes a VAT taxpayer only when making taxable supplies in Vanuatu or importing goods above the statutory threshold; supplies of digital services to non-residents outside Vanuatu are zero-rated or outside the scope of VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Vanuatu has no check-the-box or US-style hybrid entity election. Available mechanisms: (1) Voluntary VAT registration under the Value Added Tax Act [Cap 246] for an IC making only zero-rated export supplies, enabling input credit recovery and simplified compliance; (2) Conversion of an IC into a domestic company with VFSC approval, thereby losing the tax-exempt status and becoming subject to domestic corporate taxation rules (no income tax is currently imposed); (3) Maintenance of the IC's offshore status by conducting business wholly outside Vanuatu, with no local establishment, so that supplies fall outside the Vanuatu VAT net; (4) Where foreign hybrid mismatch rules apply, no specific Vanuatu election exists; the IC's statutory exemption certificate and offshore structuring are the operative protections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — governed by the Value Added Tax Act [Cap 246] and administered by the Vanuatu Revenue and Customs Department (VRCD)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VT 5,000,000 (five million Vatu) of taxable supplies in any consecutive twelve-month period; non-resident ICs supplying only zero-rated offshore digital services may nevertheless voluntarily register. Import VAT is payable at the border regardless of any turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Vanuatu does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, government-authorised e-invoicing, API-based tax clearance, or digital stamping for VAT invoices. Tax invoices may be issued in paper or electronic form provided they satisfy the content requirements of the Value Added Tax Act [Cap 246]. Customs import and export declarations are processed electronically through the ASYCUDA World customs management system, but this is not a VAT clearance mechanism. For the virtual concert metaverse, zero-rating substantiation relies on standard VAT invoices, payment gateway records (Stripe/USDC), and blockchain ticket-minting audit trails rather than any national e-invoicing infrastructure.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value Added Tax Act [Cap 246], the export of goods is zero-rated, and services are zero-rated where the recipient obtains the benefit outside Vanuatu or the service is supplied to a non-resident who is outside Vanuatu at the time of supply. For the virtual concert metaverse (ISIC 7110 / NAICS 711310), the IC's supplies of digital event access and ticket tokens qualify for zero-rating if: (i) the purchaser is a non-resident not present in Vanuatu at the time of supply; (ii) payment is received in foreign currency or USDC through offshore payment rails; (iii) the performance is delivered digitally via a global metaverse platform with no physical Vanuatu venue; and (iv) the IC maintains contemporaneous records demonstrating the offshore recipient and foreign receipt. No physical customs export declaration applies to intangible digital services; the zero-rating evidence bundle substitutes commercial and payment documentation for the customs export documentation used for tangible goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: VFSC Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing confirming International Company tax-exempt status
Executed virtual-event ticketing and access agreement together with metaverse platform terms identifying each purchaser as a non-resident outside Vanuatu
Blockchain or platform ticket-minting sales ledger evidencing issuance of virtual concert access tokens to offshore buyers
Stripe and cryptocurrency (USDC) payment gateway settlement statements showing offshore receipt in foreign currency
Bank statements and inward remittance certificates demonstrating export proceeds repatriation within 180 days
VAT-compliant zero-rated tax invoices bearing the statutory declaration of export or offshore supply
Completed VRCD zero-rating substantiation schedule and annual return reconciliations
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The VRCD may audit zero-rated claims, and retrospective assessments can claw back wrongly claimed zero-rating with interest, effectively recharacterising the supply as taxable at 12.5% VAT. Fraudulent export zero-rating or refund claims attract penalty tax of up to 200% of the tax evaded, daily default interest, criminal fines, and imprisonment for directors and other responsible persons. Failure to maintain the required documentation bundle, or failure to repatriate export proceeds within the statutory term, rebuts the zero-rating presumption and exposes the IC to full VAT assessment with penalties. As the International Company is otherwise tax-exempt, the principal compliance exposure is VAT, late-payment penalties, deregistration, and adverse VFSC regulatory findings affecting the IC's good standing.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV), established under the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu Act [Cap. 142] and operating as the monetary authority, the banker to licensed banks, and the licensing and supervisory authority for commercial banks under the Financial Institutions Act 2004. The RBV administers the exchange-rate framework for the national currency, the Vanuatu Vatu (ISO 4217 code VUV), and is flanked by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), which regulates International Companies and virtual-asset activity. Vanuatu has no separate foreign-exchange administration; foreign-exchange policy is executed entirely through RBV-authorized commercial banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu maintains a fully liberalized capital account with no exchange-control legislation, no current-account licensing, and no restriction on inward or outward remittances. The VUV is fully convertible for residents and non-residents, and the RBV operates a de facto conventional peg expressed against a trade-weighted basket comprising principally the AUD, USD, NZD, EUR, and JPY, publishing a daily official mid-rate. Profit and dividend remittances from an International Company (IC) are unrestricted; an IC is statutorily prohibited from carrying on business with Vanuatu residents and therefore repatriates exclusively to offshore counterparties. Foreign-currency accounts (USD, AUD, EUR, NZD) may be held freely by ICs, and there is no requirement to convert export or ticket-sale receipts into VUV, other than incidental settlements of bank charges and fees. Practical friction exists only in correspondent-bank KYC screening of outward USD wires and in bank-level due diligence on cryptocurrency-linked inflows, not in any RBV approval gate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None under Vanuatu law. There is no statutory timeline, minimum repatriation ratio, mandatory conversion obligation, or surrender requirement for export proceeds or foreign-currency revenue. A Virtual Concert Metaverse IC may lawfully retain 100% of ticket-sale proceeds, licensing fees, and USDC-derived fiat revenue in offshore USD accounts, offshore VUV accounts, or at an overseas EMI. Banks nonetheless impose private-contractual screening on cryptocurrency-linked inflows and may require a documented treasury policy for crypto-to-fiat conversions; these are bank policy requirements, not RBV controls, and do not alter the statutory position of full external convertibility.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Foreign-Currency Account (USD) and VUV Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-LOW for a pure Vanuatu IC. Major digital EMIs (Wise Business, Airwallex, Currenxie, Mercury, Payoneer) generally impose 12-24 months of operating history, exclude or heavily scrutinize VU-incorporated entities due to residual offshore-vehicle and correspondent-banking risk, and none accept USDC directly. A VU IC with a VFSC-licensed registered agent, CRS self-certification, and audited financial statements may secure an account with Currenxie or Airwallex through an introducing intermediary only on evidence of economic substance and clean source of funds. Stripe does not support Vanuatu-incorporated merchants; a Hong Kong or Singapore SPV is required as merchant-of-record, settling to the VU IC via intercompany MT103 transfers. Legal constraints: the Financial Institutions Act 2004 prohibits unlicensed payment institutions from holding client funds in Vanuatu, so the IC must use EMIs licensed in their own jurisdictions (FCA, ASIC, MAS, FinCEN), and must not accept card settlements into the Vanuatu domestic VUV accounts without a full CDD trail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate requires directors to appear physically in Vanuatu; the International Companies Act [Cap. 222] permits fully remote formation and offshore management. As a matter of bank policy, ANZ and BSP generally require physical or recorded video-conference KYC interviews for all non-resident directors, with notarized passport copies, apostilled board resolutions, and a certified register of directors; NBV prefers an in-branch meeting or a visit by the registered agent; BRED accepts remote onboarding with a live video interview when the VFSC-licensed registered agent co-signs the account mandate. Recommended compliance posture: convene a single board meeting in Port Vila at the registered agent's office to execute the account mandate, sign specimen cards, complete AML interviews, and present source-of-funds documentation in one session. If remote-only onboarding is unavoidable, execute an apostilled power of attorney in favor of the registered agent, supported by certified corporate documents and a recorded director interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore-vehicle opacity of a Vanuatu International Company: non-resident-owned, tax-exempt, historically associated with bearer-share and confidentiality structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current-issue IC Act certificate of incorporation; certified register of members and directors custodied by a VFSC-licensed registered agent; signed beneficial-ownership declaration naming every natural person holding 10% or more of the issued capital; CRS and FATCA self-certifications; two bank references from the beneficial owner's home jurisdiction; audited or management accounts for the previous operating period; narrative business plan explaining the Virtual Concert Metaverse model, expected volumes, and counterparty jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital-asset (USDC) receipt and crypto-to-fiat conversion without an auditable chain of custody, raising money-laundering and sanctions red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Company AML/CFT manual aligned with the VFSC Virtual Assets Service Providers Act 2022 and FATF Recommendation 15; published corporate wallet addresses used exclusively by the ticketing platform; blockchain-analytics certificates (Chainalysis or Elliptic) covering all inbound USDC flows; KYC records for ticket purchasers including name, email, IP address, and payment method; daily treasury log mapping USDC sales to fiat conversion executed through a regulated exchange or OTC desk (e.g., Coinbase Exchange or Gemini Clear); annual independent audit report on wallet control, segregation, and reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Residual country-risk flags arising from Vanuatu's prior FATF grey-listing (removed June 2021) and EU listing as a non-cooperative jurisdiction (removed February 2023).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official FATF de-listing communication; EU Council de-listing notice; VFSC certificate of good standing; evidence of economic substance in Vanuatu, including a registered-office lease at the agent's premises, current corporate register filings, and maintained accounting records at the agent's address; written confirmation of no regulatory enforcement actions against the IC or its directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between merchant settlement origin (Stripe or SPV located in the United States, Hong Kong, or Singapore) and the VU IC legal entity, creating suspicion of proxy or nominee arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed intercompany master services agreement and IP license between the SPV and VU_IC; periodic intercompany invoices traceable to ticket-sale reports; MT103 references reconciling to the SPV settlement schedule; board minutes approving the treasury routing; group treasury policy demonstrating that the SPV acts only as a payment agent while the VU IC retains economic ownership of the platform IP and controls the operating treasury.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route via SWIFT MT103 from the beneficial owner's or SPV's bank account to the VU IC account held at a Vanuatu commercial bank, with the remittance narrative 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION - SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN - VU_IC'. Vanuatu does not operate a statutory purpose-code regime, but the beneficiary bank records the stated purpose for CDD; RBV foreign-investment approval is not required because the IC is an offshore entity under the International Companies Act and no controlled-business or foreign-investment clearance attaches to it. Supporting bundle: board resolution authorizing the share issuance or loan; subscription agreement or signed loan note; source-of-funds evidence for the remitter (six months of bank statements and wealth documentation); updated register of members after allotment; confirmation that the IC faces no minimum paid-up capital requirement. USDC-denominated capital injections cannot be accepted through domestic bank rails; the USDC must first be liquidated into USD fiat at a VFSC-licensed or exchange-regime-regulated VASP before wiring to the Vanuatu account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is the SWIFT MT103 network through RBV-licensed commercial banks; USD transfers clear via correspondent banks in New York or Australia, and AUD transfers via Australian correspondents; VUV balances convert and settle domestically. Vanuatu imposes no exchange-control approval, no stamp duty on outward wire transfers, and no withholding tax at source for an IC, so full gross amounts may leave the country for content creators, licensing partners, technology vendors, and professional advisors. Commercial letters of credit under UCP600 are not required for low-risk digital services and should be reserved for high-value physical merchandise contingencies. For USDC disbursements to artists and technology vendors, use on-chain USDC clearing over Ethereum, Solana, or Stellar from the VU IC treasury wallet; fiat-bridge conversions above USD 50,000 must be executed through a regulated OTC desk, recorded in the AML/CFT log, and referenced to the corresponding on-chain transaction, never co-mingled with same-day MT103 settlement without documentary linkage. Stripe cannot settle directly to a VU IC; the offshore SPV collects card revenue locally and executes periodic intercompany MT103 settlements to VU_IC, with each payment referenced to the underlying merchant settlement statement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/VUV deliverable spot and outright forwards transacted with RBV-licensed commercial banks (ANZ, BSP, BRED), conventional tenors up to 12 months, collateralized by cash margin or interbank limits
FX swaps (USD/VUV and AUD/VUV) to manage liquidity concentration between the VUV settlement account and the USD treasury account
Cross-currency swaps (USD floating versus VUV fixed) for matched funding of medium-term capital or intercompany loan structures
Vanilla FX options (USD call/VUV put and USD put/VUV call) purchased from bank treasury desks for paid-premium hedging of large ticket-sale repatriations

Offshore Vanuatu Vatu non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) through licensed international broker-dealers, permitted where the physical VUV market is illiquid, with settlement made in a deliverable currency (USD or AUD) and counterparty limited to regulated institutions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Prescribed Annual Renewal Filing for an International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) - Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary of the date of incorporation, repeating annually until dissolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a penalty of Vt 5,000 per commenced month; continued default may lead to a compliance warning, registration of a strike-off notice, and administrative dissolution after the statutory notice period. Restoration after strike-off requires payment of reinstatement fees and VFSC approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Ownership Register Accuracy and Share Transfer Updates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed before the annual return deadline; re-confirmed within 14 days after any share transfer or change in significant control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or confirm beneficial ownership information is an offence under Vanuatu AML/CFT legislation; penalties may be imposed upon VFSC inspection, the company's good-standing certificate may be withheld, and directors or the registered agent may be subject to prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit threshold applies to a non-licensed Vanuatu International Company. An independent audit becomes mandatory only if the entity holds a VFSC licence (for example, international banking, insurance, securities dealing, or forex dealing) or if the registered agent's internal risk assessment requires audited financial statements. A virtual concert ticketing platform using standard payment processing and USDC does not create a statutory audit trigger.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is the reference framework for voluntarily prepared financial statements; Vanuatu law does not impose a separate local GAAP obligation on a non-licensed International Company. Books and records may be maintained in any substantial currency and are not required to be filed with VFSC.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: On each annual cycle, the registered agent obtains a signed director's resolution confirming that the Register of Beneficial Owners accurately identifies the natural persons with a qualifying ownership interest (generally 25% or more of shares or voting rights) and that all share transfers and control changes have been recorded. The confirmation is included in the annual return package and must be re-executed after any ownership transfer. The current register is available to VFSC and law-enforcement authorities for AML/CFT supervision.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$800 - US$1,500 per annum (covers licensed registered agent, registered office, local corporate secretary, annual return preparation, and register maintenance)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$1,500 - US$4,000 for a voluntary independent audit; US$0 if management accounts only and no licensed audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — International Companies (ICs) incorporated under the International Companies Act [Cap 222] are exempt from corporate income tax; Vanuatu levies no national corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, and no branch profits tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Effective rate 0%. ICs may obtain a tax exemption certificate under s. 99 IC Act granting exemption from all Vanuatu taxes on income and assets for the duration of the exemption period. No stamp duty on IC instruments, no withholding taxes, no payroll tax for expatriate directors, and no exchange control. VAT (12.5%) applies only to taxable supplies made within Vanuatu or to Vanuatu consumers; offshore metaverse ticketing income is outside the VAT net unless in-country consumers are served.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No annual corporate income tax return exists in Vanuatu for ICs. The operative compliance instrument is the VFSC Annual Compliance Statement (ACS), prepared and submitted by the licensed Vanuatu registered agent through the VFSC Business Paperless Portal (BPP).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned to the IC's incorporation anniversary. No quarterly income tax instalments and no estimated CIT filings apply to an exempt IC.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ACS and the annual government fee are due on or before each incorporation anniversary date. A short statutory grace period is customary; thereafter VFSC imposes late filing penalties and late fee surcharges. Failure to file and pay exposes the IC to automatic strike-off under s. 119 IC Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name of the International Company, IC registration number, date of incorporation, registered office in Vanuatu.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholder/director information is provided as registered with VFSC; the company remains a non-resident taxpayer for Vanuatu purposes and the IC must state its offshore status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification by the licensed Vanuatu registered agent that the IC has maintained its registered office, agent relationship, and statutory registers as required under the IC Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered agent signs and files the ACS; non-resident directors are not required to sign. The agent must have current know-your-customer (KYC) evidence for each beneficial owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration under s. 99 IC Act that the IC has not derived profit or income from within Vanuatu and has not conducted local business with Vanuatu residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm on behalf of the non-resident group that no Vanuatu-source revenue exists. If the IC facilitates virtual concert ticket sales to Vanuatu consumers, the declaration is inaccurate and VAT registration becomes obligatory.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharges scale with the length of delay; VFSC may compound daily penalties. Persistent non-filing results in strike-off, loss of limited liability protection for subsequent obligations, and restoration costs. The registered agent may also be sanctioned by VFSC for failure to maintain accurate compliance records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: VAT Registration and Periodic Return (Vanuatu VAT Act 2022) — conditional form. Required only when the IC supplies taxable electronic/digital services, including virtual event tickets, to persons in Vanuatu or derives Vanuatu turnover above the registration threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return and payment due within 21 days after the end of each calendar quarter. Non-resident suppliers of e-services to Vanuatu consumers must register under the non-resident VAT procedure, either directly or through a fiscal representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross consideration for virtual concert tickets, digital tokenization fees, and metaverse event access delivered to Vanuatu-located consumers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs must identify Vanuatu-based ticket purchasers using reliable geolocation/payment-billing evidence and include those supplies in Box A.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 12.5% value-added tax charge on all taxable Box A supplies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident IC must issue VAT invoices showing Vanuatu VAT registration number when supplying Vanuatu consumers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creditable VAT paid on Vanuatu-sourced business expenses directly attributable to the taxable supplies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident suppliers may offset input VAT only where the expense bears authentic Vanuatu VAT invoices and is attributable to the Vanuatu supply chain.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late registration triggers assessment of uncollected VAT plus interest; deliberate suppression of ticket revenues attracts an additional tax shortfall penalty calculated as a percentage of the evaded VAT; repeated default enables the Vanuatu Revenue Commissioner to issue penalty assessments and, in egregious cases, to restrain the IC's payment processors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% statutory dividend withholding tax — Vanuatu has no dividend withholding tax, no corporation tax on distributions, and no remittance tax. An IC may distribute profits to non-resident shareholders free of any Vanuatu withholding or final tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu maintains no comprehensive double taxation agreement (DTA) network of general application for ICs. Dividend payments are therefore not routed through conventional treaty relief. Where the shareholder's home state asserts tax, the IC must produce: (1) VFSC Certificate of Incorporation; (2) Certificate of Good Standing; and (3) a Tax Residence Certificate/Confirmation issued by the Vanuatu Ministry of Finance where the IC demonstrates central management and control in Vanuatu. The shareholder submits these documents to the foreign tax authority together with its own Form W-8BEN-E or equivalent, and the IC must also provide a certified extract of the registered agent's beneficial ownership register. In the absence of a DTA, foreign tax credits or CFC defenses depend entirely on proof of genuine Vanuatu substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on cross-border royalties and debt interest paid by a Vanuatu IC to non-residents: 0%. Vanuatu has no domestic WHT legislation applying to royalty or interest payments. Under any limited bilateral TIEA or DTA arrangement, the resulting rate remains nil or the domestic rate applies as the floor. Foreign jurisdictions may still require arm's-length substantiation for intercompany royalties in the metaverse ticketing platform, including licensing fees for virtual event IP and USDC loan interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory threshold exists — Vanuatu has no transfer pricing legislation, no OECD BEPS-aligned Local File/Master File filing obligation, and no transfer pricing penalty regime. Nevertheless, if the IC charges management fees, platform royalties, or ticket-asset licensing fees to an overseas parent or affiliate, the parent jurisdiction will apply its own thresholds (e.g., EUR 7.5 million intra-group services in the EU or USD 10 million in the US) and may request the IC's preparer-level documentation. A practical threshold: prepare contemporaneous benchmark documentation whenever annual cross-border related-party transactions exceed USD 1,000,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu has no locally codified Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) similar to the UAE/DE or Barbados regimes. However, substance is enforced indirectly through the AML/CFT Act, the VASP Act 2020, and international listing reviews. An IC operating a virtual concert ticketing business must demonstrate in Vanuatu: licensed registered agent, local registered office, board meetings or director resolutions respecting the IC's affairs, availability of accounting records, and, where digital token custody is involved, a VASP licence. Absence of real decision-making in Port Vila renders the IC a shell in the eyes of foreign CFC, GAAR, and late-tax regimes, and may trigger VASP licence denial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Foreign CFC and GAAR Exposure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the virtual concert and digital ticket tokenization business through a Vanuatu IC with 0% corporate tax while central management, contracting, directors' decisions, and digital operations remain in a high-tax jurisdiction; backdating ticket revenue invoices; omitting intercompany royalty income to divert profits artificially.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu: revocation of the tax exemption certificate, strike-off of the IC, and administrative fines for false declarations under the IC Act. Foreign jurisdictions: reclassification of the IC as a Controlled Foreign Corporation, full attribution of undistributed profit, underpayment interest, and substantial accuracy-related penalties (up to 50% of the tax shortfall in some jurisdictions).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations face personal tax assessments after piercing the corporate veil, civil restitution of diverted profits, and disqualification orders from VFSC. Where a warrant is issued by a foreign revenue authority, directors may encounter travel bans, asset freezes, and extradition-related detention.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an IC with nominee directors, no physical presence in Port Vila, no board documentation, no bookkeeping from Vanuatu, and using the zero-tax status simply to warehouse metaverse ticketing income from global fans.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VFSC administrative dissolution of the IC, restoration penalties, and forfeiture of limited liability protection for debts incurred after the shell character is established. Under the AML/CFT Act and Proceeds of Crime Act, funds routed through a shell are subject to confiscation orders; financial institutions are required to de-risk the account once shell indicators are reported.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may be jointly and severally liable for the IC's liabilities if the entity is treated as a sham; directors face fiduciary breach claims, confiscation of personal assets, and disqualification from managing any Vanuatu entity for a statutory period.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the virtual concert platform as an unregistered money/value transfer service; accepting USDC and fiat ticket payments, issuing digital tokenized tickets, engaging in token transfers between users, and failing to register as a reporting entity with the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit (VFIU) or obtain a VASP licence under the VASP Act 2020.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed VASP activity is a criminal offence under the VASP Act, punishable by significant fines and terms of imprisonment. Money laundering under the Proceeds of Crime Act carries a maximum penalty of imprisonment up to 20 years and a fine of up to VUV 100 million. VFIU may issue freezing orders against the IC's merchant accounts and crypto wallets; VFSC may revoke all registrations and prohibit the entity from further trading.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners engaging in or wilfully blind to USDC laundering face personal criminal prosecution, imprisonment, travel restrictions, and placement on the VFIU watch-list. Corporate veil-piercing applies where the IC is used as an instrument of money laundering, rendering officers personally liable for civil restitution to victims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT Evasion on In-Country Digital Supplies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling virtual concert tickets to Vanuatu residents through Stripe or direct USDC rails and treating the entire transaction as an offshore export, thereby misclassifying taxable e-services within Vanuatu and failing to charge the 12.5% VAT or register under the VAT Act 2022.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Revenue Commissioner can assess the uncollected 12.5% VAT, impose an additional tax shortfall penalty of up to 100% of the evaded VAT in aggravated cases, add statutory interest, and direct the payment processor to withhold remittances. The IC may also lose its tax exemption certificate for conducting local business without approval.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign VAT declarations concealing Vanuatu consumer ticket sales are personally liable for civil penalties; the Business Licence Act exposes unlicensed individuals to fines per day of unlicensed trading. Persistent evasion can trigger criminal conviction, restriction orders preventing departure from Vanuatu, and personal bankruptcy proceedings for restitution.
